findings.title: Trailing slash stripping is inconsistent with RFC 6265
findings.body: The change on line 213 strips a trailing slash from the cookie path (`path.rstrip("/")`), but RFC 6265 section 5.1.4 states that a cookie's path attribute should not be altered when sent to the client. The original code preserved the trailing slash by slicing up to the last slash (`path[1 : path.rfind("/")]`), which is the correct behavior for path normalization. The new code breaks compatibility with existing cookies and violates the RFC.

findings.title: Shared cookies are sent unconditionally without domain/path checks
findings.body: The new code on lines 266–268 sends all cookies from the shared cookie jar (`self._cookies[("", "")]`) without verifying domain or path constraints. This violates RFC 6265 section 5.4, which requires that cookies be filtered by domain and path before being sent. The previous implementation correctly filtered cookies, and the new code bypasses this critical security check.

findings.title: Path matching logic is removed and replaced with a flawed alternative
findings.body: The original `_is_path_match` method (lines 313–330) was removed and replaced with a simplified check on line 300 (`len(cookie["path"]) > path_len`). This new logic does not adhere to RFC 6265 section 5.1.4, which requires that the request path starts with the cookie path and that the next character is a `/` or the end of the path. The new code skips this critical validation, allowing cookies to be sent for incorrect paths.

findings.title: Unnecessary use of itertools.product for domain/path combinations
findings.body: The new code on lines 275–284 generates all possible combinations of domains and paths using `itertools.product`, which is computationally expensive and unnecessary. The original implementation iterated over cookies in a sorted manner and filtered them based on domain and path, which is more efficient and adheres to RFC 6265. The new approach creates a large intermediate list of pairs, increasing memory usage and slowing down the filtering process.

summary.problem: The cookie jar implementation violates RFC 6265 by incorrectly handling path normalization, unconditionally sending shared cookies, and replacing the path-matching logic with a flawed alternative.
summary.done_well: The changes address edge cases like no-path cookies and improve the handling of domain/path combinations. The codebase maintains its modular structure and avoids introducing new dependencies.
